<reason>B won the live comparison: spreading does not restore the core, it recruits still-working streets toward tipping, and choke-point rules are not the same as capillary protection across a wider map. A forced a real “who pays / unofficial leak” case and kept geography on the table even after a cap, but never neutralized non-linear damage, irreversibility, or the charge that a genuine volume cap makes redrawing the map unnecessary. B answered pressure more cleanly; A’s refusal to name a cap left the map looking like the actual policy.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: visitors stay in the already-tipped core because damage is not linear, while the same load spreads many quiet streets toward a first flip; enforcement works at gates, not as bakery-by-bakery policing.</best_rebuttal>
